SAVETRACK / MINT ATELIER / COMPLETE IPHONE UI REDESIGN MASTER PROMPT
Prepared for the existing SaveTrack Flutter repository on 24 October 2026, Asia/Manila.
DELIVERABLE TYPE: a detailed implementation prompt supplied as plain text.
BEGIN COPYABLE MASTER PROMPT
Act as a principal mobile product designer, interaction designer, design systems architect, and senior Flutter UI engineer.
Redesign the existing SaveTrack application into a refined, impressive iPhone-style product with the consistency of a carefully maintained Figma design system.
Use the repository as the product brief; implement the actual screens and preserve their working behavior.
Deliver coherent production UI across authentication, Today, Goals, Save Together, Planner, Reports, Profile, AI, Agent Studio, Autopilot, and supported widgets.
Keep SaveTrack's recognizable mint-green and deep-emerald identity.
Make financial information legible, daily planning effortless, and complex AI actions understandable.
Use thoughtful hierarchy, precise spacing, excellent typography, responsive composition, tactile interactions, and complete edge states.
The requested document length applies to this prompt; implementation has no arbitrary source-code line target.
Treat any example amounts, names, dates, balances, charts, and transcripts in this prompt as synthetic design fixtures.
Populate production views from the existing account-scoped services and models.
The scan behind this prompt reads all 102 Dart files in lib, containing 43,276 physical source lines at scan time.
The scan identifies 42 files with UI declarations and 22 saved golden images in test/goldens.
Saved fixture renders were visually inspected; authenticated production screens and real-device behavior were not exercised for this prompt.
Use docs/design-prompts/ui-scan-manifest.json for file hashes, class locations, UI entry points, and the saved-image inventory.
Source locations describe the scan snapshot; resolve symbols again before editing after the repository changes.
The attached earlier Mint Aurora text is background context; the repository decides whether a capability currently exists.
The repository already includes goal filtering, sorting, weekly planning, savings activity charts, and Home customization despite older README scope statements.
Design all surfaces listed below, including subviews and overlays; the inventory is not a claim that each surface is a separate route.
Native Android widgets are existing features; an iPhone visual direction does not establish a WidgetKit implementation.
Existing Android speech bridges do not establish iOS voice support; use actual platform capability checks.
Treat all precise sizes and motion timings below as proposed SaveTrack design decisions, subject to accessibility and measured layout.
Official guidance is linked in the reference appendix; custom palette values and frame sizes are this project's design specification.
===== A / DESIGN DIRECTION AND EXECUTION CONTRACT =====
[A01] 01 / Product vision
[A01.01] Make the first glance answer three questions: what I have saved, what matters next, and what I can do now.
[A01.02] Give Today a clear savings focal point with compact actions beneath it.
[A01.03] Let goals feel personal through optional covers, meaningful names, and visible progress.
[A01.04] Give Planner a calm rhythm that distinguishes dates, priorities, completion, and conflicts.
[A01.05] Let Reports explain recorded activity with exact labels and usable time windows.
[A01.06] Treat Profile as an efficient settings index with a compact identity header.
[A01.07] Keep AI advice visibly separate from Agent actions and actual savings records.
[A01.08] Use expressive mint sparingly where it draws attention to a meaningful control or value.
[A01.09] Let empty states teach one useful next step using short, encouraging copy.
[A01.10] Judge polish by the consistency of all screens, including dialogs and failure states.
[A01.11] Make the visual identity feel owned by SaveTrack through its existing logo and colors.
[A01.12] Capture a baseline before changing layout so improvements can be compared.
[A02] 02 / Existing application boundaries
[A02.01] Work inside the existing Flutter project and current app identifiers.
[A02.02] Reuse Firebase Authentication, account guards, Firestore repositories, and existing domain models.
[A02.03] Preserve exact money parsing, denominations, transaction IDs, conversion snapshots, and balance validation.
[A02.04] Retain withdrawal confirmations and all shared contribution authorization checks.
[A02.05] Retain Agent review, permissions, operation limits, approval expiry, and execution policy.
[A02.06] Respect Home preferences, featured goals, hidden sections, and saved view modes.
[A02.07] Keep reminder recurrence, timezone handling, and phone scheduling status authoritative.
[A02.08] Keep photo processing, private storage behavior, and removal permissions intact.
[A02.09] Reuse the installed Manrope font and Google sign-in brand asset.
[A02.10] Avoid backend migration, billing changes, paid services, or dependency upgrades solely for visual polish.
[A02.11] Keep actual account data separate from synthetic screenshot fixtures.
[A02.12] Report any capability requiring new backend work as a separate proposal before representing it as working.
[A03] 03 / iPhone design grammar
[A03.01] Use large titles that collapse into one compact navigation title while scrolling.
[A03.02] Use grouped settings rows with aligned labels, trailing values, and inset separators.
[A03.03] Use contextually appropriate sheets for short choices and full-height forms for longer tasks.
[A03.04] Keep a stable five-destination bottom navigation model: Today, Goals, Planner, Reports, Profile.
[A03.05] Provide a clear back path from every pushed page and a clear dismiss action on every modal.
[A03.06] Use platform-aware date/time pickers and text editing behavior.
[A03.07] Use restrained translucent navigation surfaces only where they preserve text contrast.
[A03.08] Use solid content surfaces for balances, forms, transaction reviews, and dense data.
[A03.09] Match existing navigation state and OS back behavior throughout the redesign.
[A03.10] Give primary controls tactile feedback without changing layout around a pressed item.
[A03.11] Keep real status bars and system insets under operating-system control.
[A03.12] Describe the result as iPhone-inspired Flutter UI unless native platform behavior has actually been implemented and verified.
[A04] 04 / Figma structure
[A04.01] Organize design pages as Foundations, Components, Patterns, Screens, States, Prototypes, and Handoff.
[A04.02] Name frames by area, surface, theme, width, and state; use a consistent slash hierarchy.
[A04.03] Create reusable color variables with Light and Dark modes.
[A04.04] Create text styles for display amounts, large titles, titles, body, labels, captions, and metadata.
[A04.05] Create spacing, radius, stroke, and elevation variables rather than individual magic values.
[A04.06] Build every content group with Auto Layout and intentional fill or hug behavior.
[A04.07] Use reusable component instances for buttons, fields, tabs, rows, chips, charts, and notices.
[A04.08] Use variants for state, emphasis, size, selection, theme, and platform where behavior differs.
[A04.09] Document min/max widths and text growth behavior for every reusable component.
[A04.10] Connect end-to-end prototypes for creating a goal, recording savings, planning a task, and reviewing a mission.
[A04.11] Annotate asynchronous states and real permission boundaries in prototype flows.
[A04.12] If no Figma editing surface is available, deliver the same design contracts in Flutter and annotated screenshots without claiming a Figma file was created.
[A05] 05 / Information hierarchy
[A05.01] Limit each local decision region to one visually dominant action.
[A05.02] Group facts by meaning rather than placing every fact inside a separate floating card.
[A05.03] Place labels close to their values and explanatory text close to the control it explains.
[A05.04] Use section headings to distinguish gallery, activity, reminders, and planning.
[A05.05] Place destructive operations in contextual menus or separated danger groups.
[A05.06] Let progress support amounts; preserve the balance as the main financial datum.
[A05.07] Use concise captions when a total is estimated or combines display currencies.
[A05.08] Use visible text to explain selection, disabled controls, and permission state.
[A05.09] Keep all numerical units and currency codes available at the point of interpretation.
[A05.10] Let long content scroll naturally; avoid shrinking an entire view to make it fit.
[A05.11] Use whitespace to distinguish separate decisions, with tighter spacing inside a decision.
[A05.12] Maintain the same reading order visually and for assistive technologies.
[A06] 06 / Typography direction
[A06.01] Retain Manrope as the app's brand face and use a coherent weight range.
[A06.02] Use 34 logical pixels for expanded page titles at the default text scale.
[A06.03] Use 20 logical pixels for compact navigation titles where the route geometry permits.
[A06.04] Use 38 logical pixels for featured savings amounts with adaptive wrapping.
[A06.05] Use 22 logical pixels for section titles that need strong separation.
[A06.06] Use 17 logical pixels for ordinary body copy in the proposed iPhone style.
[A06.07] Use 15 logical pixels for secondary rows and supporting labels.
[A06.08] Use 13 logical pixels for concise metadata with sufficient contrast.
[A06.09] Use tabular figures for amounts, dates, rates, and chart values where available.
[A06.10] Keep financial values readable at large text sizes by allowing reflow before reducing size.
[A06.11] Specify line-height per text role and avoid globally tight tracking.
[A06.12] Use sentence case for controls and reserve uppercase for rare short category labels.
[A07] 07 / Surface and material hierarchy
[A07.01] Use a quiet off-white mint canvas for Light mode.
[A07.02] Use white or slightly mint-tinted content panels with subtle borders.
[A07.03] Use a midnight emerald canvas for Dark mode.
[A07.04] Separate dark panels with distinct luminance and restrained borders.
[A07.05] Reserve the strongest emerald hero treatment for the most important financial or contextual region.
[A07.06] Use soft elevation only for actual overlays and floating navigation controls.
[A07.07] Keep blur clipped to its own bounds and provide an opaque fallback.
[A07.08] Give content behind translucent navigation enough scroll padding to remain readable.
[A07.09] Use strokes and spacing before adding another shadow.
[A07.10] Keep chart backgrounds flat enough that series and labels stay legible.
[A07.11] Keep photo scrims local to text placed over photography.
[A07.12] Reduce decorative effects when they impair scrolling, contrast, or recognition.
[A08] 08 / Spatial rhythm
[A08.01] Use an eight-point rhythm for major composition, supported by four-point micro-spacing.
[A08.02] Set the standard phone page inset to 20 logical pixels.
[A08.03] Use 16-pixel page insets on the narrowest supported layouts.
[A08.04] Use 24 pixels between related sections and 32 pixels between major regions.
[A08.05] Use 16 to 20 pixels of content padding inside ordinary cards.
[A08.06] Use 24 pixels of internal padding for featured financial surfaces when width allows.
[A08.07] Use 12 pixels between stacked form fields plus space for labels and validation.
[A08.08] Use 8 pixels between icons and short labels when both belong to one control.
[A08.09] Use a 20-pixel card radius and a 26-pixel featured radius as the default family.
[A08.10] Use a 16-pixel field radius and a 28-pixel modal radius where the platform allows.
[A08.11] Align repeated leading icons, title baselines, and trailing chevrons.
[A08.12] Document any exception with a specific content or interaction reason.
[A09] 09 / Navigation architecture
[A09.01] Keep all five current top-level destinations in their current order.
[A09.02] Preserve visited-tab state and per-tab scroll positions.
[A09.03] Keep offscreen animation tickers disabled using the existing lifecycle pattern.
[A09.04] Keep Assist as one clear entry that offers AI Coach and Agent Studio separately.
[A09.05] Retain account-scoped resets when the signed-in user changes.
[A09.06] Keep deep links from reminders and widgets pointed at the original record.
[A09.07] Handle unavailable records with a meaningful explanation and safe return route.
[A09.08] Use navigation transitions that match the actual platform and installed Flutter support.
[A09.09] Preserve the selected Planner date while moving between tabs.
[A09.10] Keep sheet stacks shallow so users can understand the path back.
[A09.11] Support tapping the active tab to return to its root only if implemented consistently and verified.
[A09.12] Keep navigation controls visible at large text sizes without covering page content.
[A10] 10 / Financial truth
[A10.01] Display stored goal denomination alongside important financial values.
[A10.02] Treat a preferred display currency as presentation rather than a change to saved amounts.
[A10.03] Label multi-currency totals and current-rate estimates explicitly.
[A10.04] Use the existing exact decimal parser and denomination-specific precision.
[A10.05] Keep signs, transaction direction, and contribution attribution visible.
[A10.06] Cap visual progress at the track boundary while preserving the actual numerical balance.
[A10.07] Show over-target and completed states without altering stored values.
[A10.08] Keep a projected balance labelled Preview until a confirmed record succeeds.
[A10.09] Use the locked conversion snapshot throughout one confirmed entry.
[A10.10] Represent stale or missing rates with an unavailable or stale state from the existing service.
[A10.11] Use neutral language for self-reported savings; a saved record is not a bank transfer.
[A10.12] Retain idempotent request identities when retrying financial submissions.
[A11] 11 / Forms and editing
[A11.01] Show persistent labels rather than relying on placeholders.
[A11.02] Group fields by user decision: purpose, amount, schedule, and optional details.
[A11.03] Keep the current validators and make each validation message actionable.
[A11.04] Retain typed input after failed asynchronous requests.
[A11.05] Focus the first actionable invalid field after submission validation.
[A11.06] Use appropriate keyboard types and input actions without blocking paste or accessibility.
[A11.07] Keep optional fields visibly optional.
[A11.08] Keep the save control reachable when the keyboard and accessibility text are active.
[A11.09] Use the existing unsaved-changes guard for editable records.
[A11.10] Lock duplicate submissions while the current request is in flight.
[A11.11] Use dismissible informational sheets and protected critical submission states according to actual behavior.
[A11.12] Restore focus to the invoking control after a canceled picker or dialog.
[A12] 12 / Collections
[A12.01] Preserve existing goal search, filter, sort, and presentation settings.
[A12.02] Keep query controls together above the collection.
[A12.03] Show active filter count only when it helps explain a reduced result set.
[A12.04] Distinguish an empty account from an empty search result.
[A12.05] Keep featured goal order deterministic and clearly indicate pinning.
[A12.06] Give list, grid, and gallery modes the same underlying data and actions.
[A12.07] Avoid clipped action buttons inside horizontally swiped content.
[A12.08] Use lazy rendering for long transaction, task, and mission histories.
[A12.09] Keep page size and loading controls consistent with existing repository behavior.
[A12.10] Preserve stable keys so new data does not scramble local view state.
[A12.11] Maintain access to clear-search and reset-filter actions.
[A12.12] Explain an unavailable or deleted selected record without substituting an unrelated record.
[A13] 13 / Time and planning
[A13.01] Use the user's local date and timezone for planner navigation and reminder descriptions.
[A13.02] Display actual scheduled recurrence and the next occurrence when available.
[A13.03] Keep daily and weekly modes connected to one selected date.
[A13.04] Retain midnight rollover and active-tab update behavior.
[A13.05] Keep all-day or flexible-time tasks distinct from fixed schedule windows.
[A13.06] Use priority labels as well as color.
[A13.07] Represent schedule conflicts as explainable warnings with a path to edit.
[A13.08] Avoid implying that a suggestion automatically scheduled a task.
[A13.09] Keep completion reversible only through the existing task operation.
[A13.10] Preserve reminders scoped to personal goals, tasks, or the current shared-goal member.
[A13.11] Keep disabled and invalid reminders manageable from the agenda.
[A13.12] Show OS notification permission separately from a saved in-app reminder setting.
[A14] 14 / AI and Agent distinction
[A14.01] Keep Ask Anything and Coach as separate modes with their existing sessions.
[A14.02] Keep private-context selection and approval explicit.
[A14.03] Use verified local fact cards to explain what Coach actually knows.
[A14.04] Keep general advice clearly separated from recorded account values.
[A14.05] Let Agent draft cards expose editable titles, amounts, dates, targets, and dependencies.
[A14.06] Use one strong review action before execution.
[A14.07] Preserve policy-authorized Autopilot settings without implying unlimited automation.
[A14.08] Keep financial record confirmation inside its protected existing workflow.
[A14.09] Show per-step mission outcomes and partial success honestly.
[A14.10] Keep voice transcript review distinct from sending a request.
[A14.11] Use textual status for listening, processing, speaking, and unavailable voice.
[A14.12] Offer the typed composer whenever voice support is unavailable or denied.
[A15] 15 / Accessibility foundation
[A15.01] Use at least 44 by 44 logical pixels as the proposed iPhone control target and respect larger platform requirements where applicable.
[A15.02] Measure actual rendered color contrast for text, controls, progress, and selected states.
[A15.03] Use 4.5:1 contrast for normal text and 3:1 for large text where those WCAG criteria apply.
[A15.04] Use at least 3:1 contrast for essential non-text control boundaries where required.
[A15.05] Preserve system text scaling and test at 100, 130, 160, and 200 percent.
[A15.06] Use semantic headings, labels, values, selection, toggled state, and disabled state.
[A15.07] Read monetary values with a meaningful currency code or name.
[A15.08] Make charts available through textual summaries or structured data lists.
[A15.09] Keep keyboard and screen-reader focus within an open modal.
[A15.10] Use more than color to communicate errors, withdrawals, completion, and warnings.
[A15.11] Honor reduced motion and accessibility navigation preferences.
[A15.12] Use opaque surfaces when reduced transparency or measured readability requires them.
[A16] 16 / Motion language
[A16.01] Use short, deliberate transitions that explain relationship and status.
[A16.02] Use 120 milliseconds as the initial press-feedback token.
[A16.03] Use 190 milliseconds as the initial selection-transition token.
[A16.04] Use 240 milliseconds for ordinary local transitions.
[A16.05] Use 420 milliseconds for a visible progress change when reduced motion is off.
[A16.06] Animate transform and opacity without shifting adjacent controls.
[A16.07] Keep large-title collapse connected to scroll geometry.
[A16.08] Use a modest spring for sheets only when the installed route system supports it reliably.
[A16.09] Stop offscreen repeating animation and microphone artwork when inactive.
[A16.10] Use haptics only at meaningful interaction boundaries and where supported.
[A16.11] Keep progress truthful during asynchronous work; decorative animation cannot signal completion.
[A16.12] Verify animation behavior on a real target device before claiming frame-rate performance.
[A17] 17 / Loading and synchronization
[A17.01] Use skeletons with the geometry of the content they replace.
[A17.02] Show one purposeful loading state per independent data region.
[A17.03] Keep cached content visible when the repository provides usable cached data.
[A17.04] Distinguish cached data, pending local writes, and confirmed server results.
[A17.05] Keep retry actions attached to the failed region.
[A17.06] Avoid replacing the entire account screen with an unrelated spinner for a small update.
[A17.07] Preserve image and card aspect ratios while assets load.
[A17.08] Expose progress for a long photo operation using the existing upload lifecycle.
[A17.09] Show pagination progress below the already loaded list.
[A17.10] Keep refresh labels truthful about actual service requests.
[A17.11] Use accessibility status announcements without announcing every animation tick.
[A17.12] Keep the safe dismissal behavior of each critical operation intact.
[A18] 18 / Empty, error, and offline content
[A18.01] Write short state headings that identify the missing content or failed action.
[A18.02] Give an empty account one relevant creation action.
[A18.03] Give an empty query a clear search or filter reset action.
[A18.04] Give offline cached views a concise freshness or synchronization cue.
[A18.05] Keep failed form input so the user can retry with confidence.
[A18.06] Use permission explanations that identify the affected capability.
[A18.07] Use service-setup explanations only for real configuration failures.
[A18.08] Keep developer diagnostics out of ordinary product copy.
[A18.09] Use a stable return path when an item was deleted or access changed.
[A18.10] Treat unknown monetary values as unavailable rather than zero.
[A18.11] Retain successful mission results when a later step fails.
[A18.12] Prefer helpful recovery actions to decorative state illustrations.
[A19] 19 / Authentication presentation
[A19.01] Use the actual SaveTrack logo above a concise sign-in heading.
[A19.02] Prioritize the form on narrow phones and retain the existing wide composition where appropriate.
[A19.03] Keep email and Google sign-in options visible and clearly labelled.
[A19.04] Retain the official Google mark and provider behavior.

[A20.02] Use initials and branded geometric fallbacks when no image exists.
[A20.03] Keep landscape goal-cover framing distinct from circular avatar cropping.

===== C2 / CONCRETE ART DIRECTION AND PHONE COMPOSITIONS =====
[C.art.001] REFERENCE COMPOSITION AND VISUAL IDENTITY
[C.art.002] Use a 390 by 844 logical-pixel reference frame for the main portrait design review; this is a design canvas rather than a claim about a specific iPhone model.
[C.art.003] Create companion 320 by 693, 375 by 812, and 430 by 932 review frames to expose width and height constraints.
[C.art.004] Let real safe areas determine top and bottom system space; avoid copying an arbitrary status-bar height into production layout.
[C.art.005] At the 390px reference width, the default 20px page insets produce a 350px content column.
[C.art.006] Use a restrained palette distribution: quiet canvas and solid panels dominate, while emerald establishes priority and mint marks interaction.
[C.art.007] Keep light-theme panels clean white with a subtle green edge; avoid tinting every nested element the same pale mint.
[C.art.008] Make dark mode deliberately layered: canvas darkest, grouped surfaces slightly lighter, editable inputs distinct, and active controls luminous.
[C.art.009] Use the logo's existing geometry as the identifying visual motif instead of introducing unrelated sparkle decorations throughout the app.
[C.art.010] Keep the strongest decorative treatment in one local region at a time, such as a savings hero or a cover photograph.
[C.art.011] Use two-dimensional clarity for most screens; reserve optical depth for actual navigation, modal layering, and important state changes.
[C.art.012] Make primary action shapes consistent across finance, planning, and AI even when their semantic roles differ.
[C.art.013] Make icon stroke, corner treatment, and apparent size consistent rather than mixing several unrelated icon aesthetics.
[C.art.014] Use exact content widths and natural text height to produce composition; avoid absolute positioning of body content.
[C.art.015] Define the before/after difference in a review board: tighter decision hierarchy, less repeated promotional content, clearer data, and more coherent interactions.

===== K / OFFICIAL REFERENCE NOTES =====
Reference notes below explain external design guidance. Project token values, proposed geometry, and screen-specific decisions are authored SaveTrack recommendations.
Apple materials guidance describes Liquid Glass for controls and navigation and discusses adapting to accessibility settings: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/materials
Apple layout guidance provides the platform layout reference used when reviewing safe areas and adaptable composition: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout
Apple typography guidance is the platform typography reference; this prompt keeps the repository's Manrope branding: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography
Apple UI design tips recommends controls measuring at least 44 by 44 points; this prompt uses 44 logical pixels as a proposed Flutter iPhone-style baseline: https://developer.apple.com/design/tips/
Figma's Auto Layout guide explains responsive frame sizing including hug/fill behavior; use it to organize reusable design frames: https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040451373-Guide-to-auto-layout-in-Figma
Flutter's Cupertino library documents iOS-style controls and route primitives; confirm the installed SDK supports the specific API before adopting it: https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/cupertino/
Reference check date: 24 October 2026, Asia/Manila.
These references support design decisions; they do not establish that this repository supports every native Apple visual effect or platform service.
Use the app's actual platform capabilities and test the implemented result.
